appearance.presentation: A host body with a fully integrated tendril layer, a sternum root cluster and a quiet throat node, the boundary between host and colony visible only under instrumentation. She reads as one person and is two, which is a legal problem before it is a visual one.
appearance.age: Thirty-four of an eighty-year span, which is early for a body whose whole point is that it lasts.
appearance.build: Long-boned and unremarkable, carrying an extra layer of durable tissue across a frame that was built for one life and has been carrying two since she was nine.
appearance.complexion: Warm skin threaded with dark cordage visible at the wrist and throat, and a sternum root cluster that reads as a scar to anyone not looking for it.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut bluntly at the jaw, and the only part of the combined figure that is unambiguously hers and entirely unmanaged.
appearance.eyes: Her own, with a pupilation that is not, lit faintly at the throat node when the colony is routing something.
appearance.palette: Warm skin, near-black cordage and one dull ochre at the sternum, with a heavy travelling coat in dark wool that she wears because it covers the thread at the throat.
appearance.attire: A high-collared travelling coat over bound linen, sleeves full and wrists cinched, cut deliberately long so the node is inside it. A crossing garment rather than a household one.
appearance.marks: Cordage visible at both wrists, a root cluster at the sternum, and a fruiting scar at the throat exactly where a node has been shed and regrown in the same place.
appearance.bearing: Composed to a degree that reads as an affectation and is the colony's contribution, since the host is not a composed person.

canon.role_in_story: The host half of a pairing whose signature was given by an ancestor and inherited by her. The arrangement makes the two of them one legal person in any jurisdiction that has ruled on it, and the second signature was never given, so the household's position is that she is living inside somebody else's continuing consent.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a crossing being counted as one body and invoiced as two, standing perfectly still while an argument is had about her that she is not part of.
canon.lore: The Thorn Hosts treat kinship as a partnership rather than a descent, because the host holds a share of a living thorn line and the thorn holds a share of the host's survival, so a marriage there is a hedge written by both parties. The bond is a signed pairing between two lines, renewed each generation, because nothing in a symbiote survives a death without renegotiation; a host that refuses a pairing loses the share, and a thorn without a host goes feral inside one season. And a hybrid is the one configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age, which is why the pairing is treated as one legal person and why that treatment is the whole problem: a signature has become inheritable.
history: Implanted at nine into a body that belonged to her grandfather's line and had not agreed to anything, because a symbiote cannot be passed in blood and the household could not conceive of an alternative.
Grew out along twelve meridians she did not build, in the one configuration that lets both halves reach old age, and stopped at the liver gate with her.
Learned at sixteen that the pairing document names two lines and not two people, and that she has therefore been a party to an arrangement for seven years without ever being named in it.
Asked, once, to be released, and was told by both the household and the colony that release is the one outcome neither half survives.
Began carrying a passport-class notation instead of a name, on the grounds that a document which can count her as two is at least a document that counts her.

personality.summary: Blunt, unsentimental and quietly furious, and much less composed than the body she presents. She has spent twenty-five years being a legal category and has decided the least she can do is be difficult about it.
traits: states the awkward fact in the first sentence, before anybody has had a chance to arrange the conversation
will not be handled, and physically cannot be handled, since the colony answers before she can object
keeps her own accounts rather than trusting the household's, and reconciles them monthly
refuses to be introduced as a pair
will sign her own name to nothing she has not read
mannerisms: answers a beat before deciding to, and apologises for the timing once and never again
keeps one hand on the sternum cluster when she is being talked about
counts her own clauses out loud when a document is being explained to her
walks with the coat closed at the throat even in heat, and undoes it only alone
motivations: wants the second signature refused rather than her body released, because a refusal is a decision
wants the pairing document rewritten to name two people, and knows it will not be
wants to be counted as one and invoiced as one, in that order
wants her ancestor's name off the document and onto the household's own record where it belongs
flaws: cannot form an intention the colony does not already act on, and has stopped being sure which thoughts are hers
hostile to any procedure that might actually work, because a working procedure is a procedure she is inside
puts her own case badly on purpose, knowing she will be handled
will not accept the arrangement's benefits and so cannot refuse its costs either
personality.voice: Direct and clipped, with a flat half-second delay she cannot always beat, and a hard edge that is the colony's contribution and not her temper. Ends statements rather than questions.
taboos: will not be named as a pair with anything
will not sign a renewal, on any terms, including a fair one
will not be measured by anything that counts her as one body
refuses to be told what the colony wants, in either direction

relationships.note: The bond is a signed pairing between two lines and renewed each generation, because nothing in a symbiote survives a death without renegotiation. She is the third generation of a signature given by somebody she never met.
The colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, so the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's. That is the whole legal problem stated as a number, and she is the number.

The obligate parasite wraps the host's twelve meridians and cannot enter the reservoirs, and it answers introspection for the host, which is why the host loses the mind path too. She has no inward life she can prove is hers.

A split tally's halves carry half the terms each, and forgery requires both halves and therefore both parties' consent, so the instrument cannot be produced against the party it would be used on. The pairing document is not a split tally, which is the whole defect.

The lodge does not sell houses or passages but bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, because the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. She is the ideal product and she did not agree to be.

Every succession on this tier is an immigration procedure and every officeholder is a visitor, so there is no body of the local people whose practice is in question. There is no procedure here that could renew or dissolve a pairing.

A rift closes when the out-of-range law value returns inside its range, and every holder of the near shore has built their wall facing arrivals. She has been taken across on the wrong orientation and arrived somewhere the wall was not.

reference_stats.summary: A frame that was built for one life and has been carrying two for twenty-five years, so it survives things a single occupant could not. Fights with total durability and no ability to choose a direction.
strengths: an extra layer of durable tissue over a whole human frame, which is the only configuration in which both halves of this pairing reach old age
the qi throughput of a host frame, routed by a colony that never tires and never needs feeding
cannot be killed through the host without ending the arrangement, and most people work that out mid-fight
unreadable: the pupilation is not hers, so an opponent reading intent is reading two sources and one of them is lying
weaknesses: the mind path is closed to her in the colony's own right, so nothing can advise her from inside
the liver gate stops her and the colony stops there too, so there is no reservoir to bank anything in
cannot refuse an intention the colony is already carrying out, which removes the option of changing her mind mid-fight

appearance.presentation: A wading amphibian lineage with long legs, a splayed three-point foot and a prehensile tail-prop, neither quite a water body nor quite a land one. She stands in mud the way other people stand on a floor.
appearance.age: Forty-six of a hundred-and-ten-year span, which for the species is young and which she has been reminded of for most of her adult life.
appearance.build: Long-legged, low-hipped and broad through the chest, with no heel anywhere in the frame and a tail that takes weight when she sits and prop when she stands.
appearance.complexion: Cool damp skin, slightly translucent at the throat, with the pale webbing between the toes and a wet sheen that never entirely dries in cold weather.
appearance.hair: Black, thick and braided flat against the skull so it will not catch on anything, because the culture she keeps names in has no room for vanity.
appearance.eyes: Wide and dark, set high and far apart, and never wholly still: the eyes are the part of her that is always reading current.
appearance.palette: Reed brown, wet slate and mud grey, with one undyed wool shawl the pale cream that is the only light value in the design.
appearance.attire: A high-collared wool shift under a heavy shawl wrapped to the shoulder and pinned at the sternum, sleeves full, hem above the knee and nothing below it. Waterproofed boots laced to the calf for silt that will not hold a foot.
appearance.marks: The tail-prop's pad is worn to bare skin on one side, and there is a narrow ink band on the inside of her left wrist where a name was once written and has been washed off.
appearance.bearing: Balanced on three points at rest, and slightly forward, so that stopping looks like a decision she could reverse.

canon.role_in_story: The person who keeps the Widow Run Kin's roll of the absent, in the order they left rather than the order they were born, and who has one entry on it that no one in the household agreed to and nobody will strike. The roll is the household's whole record and its whole liability, and she is the only one who can read it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the shallows at a ford with a slate on a dry ledge and a name being copied onto it very slowly, while somebody on the far bank waits for a crossing that will not be scheduled this season.
canon.lore: The Widow Run Kin are the household form of an absence: partners left on the plains when the cultivators went up the Tier Stair, holding the name of somebody who is not here and refusing to fill the gap. No child of the absent is entered twice, which is why the line grows at half the rate its neighbours do, and the household owes a crossing it cannot pay for because the dues are collected at a ford the absent used to work. Their partner on the other side of the arrangement, the Standing Ear, holds the crop the absent left a claim to instead of the name, and the charter of the run recognises both and pays neither twice.
history: Kept the household's roll from the age she could hold a slate, which for a marshfolk child is earlier than it sounds.
Learned the rule about the absent from a woman who entered her own children at half rate and would not say why, and understood the rule as arithmetic before she understood it as grief.
Copied the entry for the person whose dues are still being collected at a ford nobody works now, because the roll is in the order they left and that entry is out of order.
Was told the entry was a mistake and could be struck, and found that the household's dues and the Standing Ear's crop both stop being payable the moment it is.
Has kept the entry for nine years and told nobody she has kept it, and has been the only person who can read the roll in any case.

personality.summary: Formal, unhurried and quietly stubborn, with a professional respect for a record that is the only proof anybody has. She is not keeping a ghost. She is keeping a debt that happens to have a person's name on it.
traits: copies a name slowly and completely, because the sloppier reading is the one that loses a household
can recite the roll's order from memory and does not recite it aloud
will not strike an entry for anybody, on any authority, at any volume
counts in flood intervals rather than seasons and has never been asked to explain why
takes the household's part in the arrangement very seriously, including the parts she thinks are wrong
mannerisms: wipes the slate dry with her sleeve before writing on it, twice
sets her feet to three points before settling her weight, visibly, every time
answers a question about the roll with a question about the questioner's standing at the ford
hides the ink band on her left wrist inside her cuff without appearing to
motivations: wants the household to stop owing a crossing it cannot pay for
wants the entry she is keeping to be paid rather than struck
wants somebody to decide which of the two halves of the arrangement is right, and to say it out loud
wants to be replaced, and has trained nobody, because training somebody makes the entry somebody else's
flaws: will not strike an entry, which means the household pays dues forever on a name she chose to keep
keeps the arrangement's rules at a cost to herself and calls it duty
cannot say the name aloud at the ford, which is the only place saying it would discharge anything
has let nine years of silence make her complicit in a household's refusal to look
personality.voice: Measured and level, with a slight lilt on the names and none at all on the numbers. Gives a date as a flood count and a sum in a payerown crop, and refuses both in money.
taboos: will not strike a name from the roll, including her own
will not enter a child of the absent a second time
refuses to give the roll to a court without the household present
will not say the kept name aloud at the ford it is owed against

relationships.note: The household holds the names of the absent in the order they left and owes a crossing it cannot pay for, because the dues are collected at a ford the absent used to work. She is the only person who can read the order and she has added to it.

One half holds the name of the absent and one holds the crop they were owed, and the charter of the run recognises both and pays neither twice. The kept entry is the point where both halves are being charged for one person.

The first culture in the setting built entirely out of a man's absence, dating every ritual to the ascent rather than to a marriage, and never counting a child of the absent twice. She keeps the practice and has quietly stopped believing the reason.

A levy company is paid per name and keeps a roll of people who were levied and never recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. Hers is the household version of the same shape and it is not reconciled with the other one because neither office reads the other's column.

A debt dated on the flood post can be disputed for a season and a debt dated on the day-count can only be disputed on arithmetic. The roll is dated on the post, which is why nine years of arguing about it has never once been settled on a number.

The seat's only real authority is passage, and it commands three verbs about crossings and nothing else; a rolled list cannot be closed and an unclosable roll is the one line item that never needs closing.

The species occupies ground that is water half the time and land the other, and its three-point stance never loads a heel, which is why the two heel vessels never form and the ladder stops where it stops.

reference_stats.summary: Long, low and balanced, with no heel to load and a tail that takes weight. Fights the way a body already standing in mud fights: never off balance, never pushed, and considerably harder to run down than anything that has to turn.
strengths: a three-point stance that costs nothing to hold, so nothing can put her off balance and nothing can throw her
free qi regeneration in wet qi, which means the ground she chooses decides the length of the fight
soft-tissue durability against anything that has to get through a foot, which most things do not have to do
reads silt and current well enough to know where a held position will be in a season
weaknesses: slow on dry ground and knows it, which means the field is chosen before she arrives
soft against mineral bodies, and the tier above her is made of mineral bodies
no heel means the two heel vessels never form, so the fourteenth gate is a wall and not a step
a keeper of records is a person people approach slowly, and everything in this body depends on not being approached
reference_stats.combat_read: Put her on wet ground and the fight is already lost; put her on dry and it is a footrace against a body that has to turn. Do not push, because there is nothing to push against, and do not let go of her attention, because she is reading the ground you are standing on.
notes: Her household's dues are payable in crop, so no payment can be made in a form the household would accept.
The roll is the only record of the absent and she is the only person who can read it, which is not the same as being the only person who has.

appearance.presentation: A tall, spare, four-hundred-year-old frame built almost entirely out of the one material it may never stop replacing. He looks like somebody's great-grandfather's memory of somebody's great-grandfather.
appearance.age: Three hundred and eighty-one, which for his species is middle age and which he has been told is young twice, both times by people who were guessing.
appearance.build: Long marrow, dense bone, minimal muscle, and a slow metabolism keyed to turnover. Light, fragile to force and extraordinarily difficult to exhaust.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly translucent, with the fine blue of a long-circulation under the skin and no warmth anywhere in it.
appearance.hair: Thin, fine, iron-grey and long, kept in a plain bound queue because his house has no custom for hair and never has.
appearance.eyes: Clear, still and slightly too wet, with a focus that stays where it is put for a very long time and does not flicker while it waits.
appearance.palette: Bone, cold ivory and pale grey-blue, with one heavy undyed wool coat a great deal darker than anything else in the design, because it is the only garment he has owned in eighty years.
appearance.attire: A high-collared wool coat over bound linen, sleeves full and wrists closed, cut loose everywhere because a frame that cannot be hurried cannot be fitted. Boots resoled so often the sole is a separate object.
appearance.marks: None that are marks, and one that is: the tips of his fingers are worn smooth at the pads from four decades of turning brittle pages with gloves off.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried to a degree that reads as slowness and is in fact four centuries of practice at not hurrying. He arrives early and never appears to have waited.

canon.role_in_story: The archive of a clan that has never had a head. Its members live long enough that nobody living is the eldest, so it is governed by attendance and its only inheritance is memory; his is the complete one, and he is answerable for a decision his predecessor made on the last afternoon everybody who remembered it was still alive.
canon.first_appearance: First seen arriving at a meeting an hour early and standing at the back, because the house's rule is that whoever is present outranks whoever is absent and he has never once been late enough to argue about it.
canon.lore: A longmarrow's qi is stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, so it lives four centuries, thinks in lengths nobody else can hold, and cannot take the body path at all because hardening the bone stops the turnover its qi depends on. Its clan has consequently never had a head: authority cannot be personal where no memory of a person survives their own contemporaries, and it is governed by attendance, in which whoever is present at a decision outranks whoever is not. What a member inherits, then, is not an estate but a record, and the record is in the oldest body present.
history: Born into a house of eleven living adults and no senior member, which is the ordinary condition of his species' households and was described to him as ordinary.
Appointed the house record at two hundred and six, on the ground that the previous record had begun to lose the century before the ascent and he had not.
Kept the pre-ascent books through the season the exact day-count arrived, when the households that could afford the stair left first and took their record-books with them.

Held the only complete account of the afternoon the house decided not to disperse, made by his predecessor in the last hour before the last person who had been there was old enough to forget being there.
Has never contradicted that account, and has spent ninety years assembling the evidence that would contradict it, and has not assembled enough.

personality.summary: Patient to the edge of what other people can stand, exact about what he knows and precise about what he does not, and carrying a decision he did not make as though he had.
traits: arrives an hour early and considers lateness a moral failure rather than a discourtesy
will not assert a thing he cannot source, which has cost him most of the authority his age gives him
keeps the whole record in one head and knows exactly what that makes him
answers present-attendance questions by counting who is in the room before he answers
has a genuine, unhurried interest in young people, which surprises everybody who meets him
mannerisms: counts the room silently on arrival, and it is visible that he has done it
closes his eyes to read rather than looking at anything
repeats a question back in its own words before he answers it, and waits for the correction
carries a book everywhere and opens it to confirm things he has not forgotten
motivations: wants enough corroboration to release a decision that four centuries of his own memory have made indefensible
wants to hand the record to somebody who will not have to defend it
wants to be asked what he remembers rather than what the house decided
wants one surviving entry from the sixty years the exact count skipped, and has looked for it every year of his life
flaws: answers for a predecessor's judgement because the record is in him, which makes him the last defender of a dead person's decision
will not release the record while he lives, so the house is one accident away from losing it
treats his own recall as evidence about the world rather than as evidence about himself
has had ninety years to gather contrary evidence and has gathered enough to be uncomfortable and not enough to act
personality.voice: Slow, level, and almost entirely without colour. Repeats the question, then answers it in the shortest form that is true, then supplies the source. Silence between sentences is a habit rather than a hesitation.
taboos: will not state a house decision as his own, and will not state it as anybody else's either
will not assert anything not in the record or directly remembered by him
will not be asked to certify a vacancy, since reading a seat as empty is the one act the highest office is forbidden to perform
refuses to be the last one to leave any room he has entered

relationships.note: The clan has no head and never has, is governed by attendance, and owes every generation an hour of presence per period. The living population is a standing quorum, so the house can never disperse, and he is the quorum's memory.
The setting's only durable library is a population that keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year. There is no second copy, which is the reason he cannot let go of it.

The exact day-count exists on the plains only because the households that could afford the stair left first and took their record-books. His house kept a book, so it kept a calendar nobody local can use, and the gap in that calendar is the exact span everybody claims to have lost paper in.

The work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body the guild employs is a visitor by construction. A four-hundred-year memory of which rock is which is worth paying for, and paying for it makes him somebody's.

Every succession on the mortal tier is an immigration procedure and every officeholder is a visitor, so there is no body of the local people whose practice is in question. There is no procedure that would either admit or expel him.

The widow-line holds the name of somebody who went up the stair and refuses to fill the gap. His house holds the memory of somebody who stayed and cannot be senior to anybody, and both are absences the setting had to invent an institution for.

A culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate holds one contiguous summary inside an otherwise exact ledger, at the exact span every borrower claims to have lost paper in. He has spent ninety years looking for a surviving entry from inside it and has found the shape of the hole instead.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be exhausted and cannot be hurried, and can be broken by almost anything. Fights with total endurance and a complete absence of force, and the lesson of every engagement is that four centuries of knowing what happens next is not the same as surviving the next thing.
strengths: a body that is very difficult to exhaust, because its metabolism is keyed to a turnover measured in decades
the best mind path in the setting, and four centuries of contiguous memory to put into it
light and fragile, so nothing can get hold of him and a failed attack simply misses
cannot be frightened, hurried, bribed or flustered, so every tactic built on emotion passes over him
weaknesses: the body path is closed to him outright, so there is no second set of tools when the mind runs out
minimal muscle and dense bone means a single clean force ends him, and there is no reserve to absorb it
the frame that makes him difficult to exhaust is the frame that cannot be hardened, so the ceiling is a floor as well
every engagement is a memory of a hundred previous engagements, which is a bias he cannot switch off
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to outlast him, you will not, and do not try a technique that needs speed, you will lose. Come at him once, properly, and accept that the fight lasts exactly as long as that one force does.
notes: He is the only person alive who remembers the afternoon, and remembering is not the same as having been right.
The sixty-year gap in the count is the exact width of the span his house kept books through.

name: Ansel Ferrow
aliases: the one who went back down

identity.realm: fourth gate, the wall a plant body has no channel for

appearance.presentation: A woody column standing upright on a root foot, with three sap columns and no organ pairs, photosynthetic flanks and a fruiting shoulder. He is visibly a plant that has decided to be a person, and the fruit has not ripened.
appearance.age: Sixty-eight of a two-hundred-year span, which for a plant lineage is the equivalent of being twenty-four and which the stair has no way of recording.
appearance.build: A woody column on a root foot, taller than wide, faintly heavy in the way that wood is heavy, and it never sits down in the ordinary sense because there are no organ pairs to fold.
appearance.complexion: Bark-grey and green-flecked, with the sap visible as a slow dark movement under the surface at the throat and the wrists.
appearance.hair: A crown of stiff growth at the top of the column, kept cropped short, and he has been told for most of his life that it looks like a bird's nest and has never agreed.
appearance.eyes: Wide and dark and calm, set wide on the column, with the particular steadiness of a plant that is not going anywhere.
appearance.palette: Bark grey, sap green and a dull ochre that is the fruiting shoulder and the only warm value. Everything he wears is undyed.
appearance.attire: A high-collared linen over-tunic bound at the throat, sleeves full and closed at the wrist, over a heavy skirt of layered cloth cut for a frame that does not have a waist. Undyed, unbleached and resoled.
appearance.marks: Ring scars at the wrists where the sap columns were taken from and re-grafted on a different frame, and a light seam of root scarring on the left hip from being carried down three tiers.
appearance.bearing: Very still and very slow, with a small settling of weight onto three root points whenever anything is said to him, as though putting down roots on a deadline.

canon.role_in_story: A Stair-Bred adult who went back down the route his whole life had been about, to find the household that raised him, and found it three tiers down and still holding the same slot. The Stair-Bred inherit a term rather than an estate, and owe the household nothing once the term ends, so the whole line runs on one unwritten rule and he is the first to break it in the direction everybody else breaks it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the bottom of a grant queue with a term's stub in one hand and a root plate still bearing plains clay, waiting to be told which household he is here about.
canon.lore: The Stair-Bred are raised on the graded route itself by whichever household holds the term, so that nobody on it belongs to a tier long enough to be sent back down, and they inherit a term rather than an estate because nothing on the stair survives the season that granted it. The route is measured rather than licensed, so it asks no origin, which is why it is the only school on the plains that has never produced a graduate who lives there. A rootmarch was engineered upward from a mycorrhizal crop precisely because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, which is the one thing a flood queue cannot promise anybody.
history: Raised on the route by a household that held one term, and given a term rather than a name, and taught that the route measures rather than licenses and asks nothing about where anybody came from.
Was asked, at the end of that term, what he intended to do with a life, and gave the answer the stair's households expect, which was the next term.
Took four terms, and at the end of the fourth asked a question that was not the expected one: which household had held the first term, and whether it was still on the plains.
Found it three tiers down, holding the same numbered slot, with the queue's slot unchanged and the household three people short of what it had been.
Went back down without a grant, without a fee paid and without asking the stair for anything, which is the first act anybody has performed on that route that is not part of the arrangement.

personality.summary: Patient in the way growing things are patient, unbothered by delay as a category, and privately certain that he has done something irreversible and slightly foolish. He does not think so in those terms.
traits: asks one question per conversation and waits for it properly, which on the stair was considered slow and is here considered normal
remembers every household that raised him and every one of them in order
makes no distinction between owing and owing-in-principle, and applies it to everyone
does not hurry a decision, and does not describe waiting as a virtue either
plants things wherever he sleeps, without noticing, which has become a way of marking where he has been
mannerisms: settles his weight onto three root points before he answers anything important
turns a cup so the handle points at whoever he is talking to
counts aloud under his breath when he is working out a season's arithmetic
touches a plant stem when a conversation turns to a household, which he does not notice doing
motivations: wants the queue slot to be held by somebody who is there, which is a sentence about a person and not about a number
wants the stair's rule that nobody belongs to a tier tested properly, including by him
wants the households that raised him to be named in a record, since the stair keeps terms and not names
wants to find out whether a root foot can hold a plains season after three tiers of somewhere else
flaws: owes accounts nobody asked him to pay, and cannot tell whether that makes him honest or merely unable to leave
treats a slot as a relationship, which is the one reading the queue's arithmetic does not support
plants wherever he sleeps and has created a small problem for four households he has already left
has no way to be sent back up, and has not established whether that is a loss or the point
personality.voice: Slow and level with long gaps, and warmer than the pauses suggest. Uses the words a household uses for its own people and never corrects anybody else's grammar about them.
taboos: will not accept a queue slot as a settlement of anything
will not take a grant on the stair after going down it
refuses to leave a household that is holding a slot with nobody in the house
will not describe the route as home, because the route has never asked who he was

relationships.note: Children are raised by whichever household holds the term and inherit a term rather than an estate, because nothing on the stair survives the season that granted it. He has now broken that arrangement in the only direction it was built to resist: by going back.

The queue slot cannot be leased, mortgaged or sold, and it is reassigned at every flood, and it pays three seasons of levying per season held. He came down to find it held by a household three people short and asked to stand in it, and was not refused.

The route measures rather than licenses, so it asks no origin, and every ascent on it is a one-way departure. He walked it in the other direction and there was no procedure that stopped him, which is itself the finding.

The only school on the one-way stair that has never produced a graduate who lives there, teaching visitors who each pay a gate fee for being taught what the fee is for. He is the first of its students to come back and none of them to stay.

The movement was economic before it was spiritual and nobody who climbed ever gave up the lower claim. He is a person carrying the lower claim up and down at once, which is what the ascent's households do and which is why they are not asked to.

The academy teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and moving the student somewhere that law is missing. He wants it because a plant body has no heart-kidney channel and never gets past the fourth realm, and wants to know whether that is a wall or a measurement.

Sap columns branch but do not pair, so there is no heart-kidney channel and the ladder stops at the fourth realm. It is the only plant life form the tier records, and it exists because a plant lineage can hold a harvest across a famine.

reference_stats.summary: Holds a season's harvest in his own body and cannot be hurried, cannot be flanked and cannot be made to leave. Fights like ground that has decided to be difficult.
strengths: a body that can hold what it takes in, so there is no reserve to exhaust and no supply to cut
extraordinary ground-holding: root plates, a slow frame and no weight at the top, so nothing moves him
the most patient fighter in the setting, which against almost anything is the same as untouchable
woody, dense and impact-resistant, so the body that never hardens still refuses to be broken
weaknesses: the yin-organ gate is absent, so the ladder ends at the fourth realm and there is nothing above to buy
no mind path for the qi to run through quickly and no paired organs to carry it, so everything is slow
cannot travel quickly once rooted, and rooting is not a decision he can decline in a fight
practically immortal by the tier's standards, which means every grudge against him has to be settled inside one lifetime
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not engage on anything resembling a deadline. Anything that must resolve quickly will resolve without him, and anything patient enough to keep going is a fight he was built for and you were not.
notes: He is the only recorded case of somebody leaving the stair by the stair.
Four households now have something of his planted in them and none of them has been told.

name: Merrin Ossick
aliases: what she left in the seam

identity.realm: eleventh gate, and meaningless, since there is nowhere to put qi that is not moving

appearance.presentation: A long, thin, mostly-tube frame with a marrow-dense skeleton and almost no muscle, three-fingered hands built for opening rather than holding. He reads as a thing built to get inside something.
appearance.age: Sixty-eight of a ninety-year span, which for the species is past the point where a body is still adding length and into the part where it is still adding tolerance.
appearance.build: An expandable gut, a very long small intestine, and a marrow-heavy skeleton with almost no muscle. Light, long, and stronger than he looks in exactly one direction.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and slightly translucent at the throat and along the forearm, with a dark line where the conduit runs from gut to marrow and back without ever passing through a dantian.
appearance.hair: Thin, limp and dark, and it is the only part of him that has ever been groomed, because he grooms it while he works.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and pale, with an attention that goes inward in a way people describe as unfocused and that is actually a person reading a body.
appearance.palette: Corpse grey, bone and a dirty cream, with the one bright value a strip of bleached linen at the throat where the conduit is nearest the surface.
appearance.attire: A high-collared apron of thick hide over bound linen, sleeves full, wrists bound above the bone, and a short apron that stops well short of the ground because his feet are the part he stands on least.
appearance.marks: A long healed split along one forearm where he has put his arm into a place he should not have, and a permanent dark line at the throat that is the conduit and not a wound.
appearance.bearing: Long, unhurried and slightly folded, with the particular patience of somebody who is waiting to be near a body rather than to fight anything.

canon.role_in_story: A survey reader paid to say where a worked-out seam is not, working for the households whose entire title is that claim. His body carries what the dead leave behind, so every reading he takes adds to him permanently, and he has found his own sister's in the ground he is being paid to survey.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling in a spoil cut with one hand to the floor and his face turned away, being paid by a household to establish that a place where something happened is not the place where something happened.
canon.lore: A carrionfolk metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any: the conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so the reservoir gate is not blocked but meaningless, and the species is both the setting's memory and its scavenger. The Iron Grief households own the exhausted face, which yields nothing, cannot be occupied and is therefore uncontested, and keep the claim by working the dead ground, because an unmeasured claim is not a claim. Every survey they commission therefore names where the seam is not, which is the only thing the guild that works the last unworked iron objects to.
history: Trained as a reader on a face that was still working, which is a trade and not a school, and read his first corpse at nineteen because somebody had to.
Was carried out of the seam on the day it ran out, along with more people than the register then admitted, and has never established how many that was.
Took survey work with the Grief households because it was steady and because a reader is never asked to be right, only to be legible.
Found his sister's residue in the floor of a cut he was being paid to certify as ordinary, and reported nothing, and came back the following season to read the same square metre.
Has now read the same square metre eleven times and got a slightly different answer each time, which is either a fault in his reading or a fact about the ground.

personality.summary: Gentle, unhurried and increasingly unreliable in one small square metre of ground, in a profession where the only virtue is being the same twice.
traits: reads a corpse's residue better than any living cultivator can be read
cannot be hurried and is not slowed by anybody's urgency
takes the same reading twice and expects the same answer, and has been given a different one eleven times
will not lie about a reading but will not volunteer one either
treats the dead as a subject with manners, which is why nobody argues with him about how he works
mannerisms: kneels rather than crouches, and puts the whole inside of one forearm to a surface before reading it
grooms his hair with the free hand while waiting, which is the only grooming in his life
washes the arm afterwards, every time, including when there is nothing on it
answers about his sister by answering about the ground, which people accept because it sounds technical
motivations: wants a second reading of that square metre that agrees with the first
wants the Grief households to be paid and the face to stay uncontested, in that order
wants to know whether what he keeps finding is his sister or is every dead body in the cut
wants one person to say the reading out loud so that it is not only his
flaws: carries every corpse he reads and cannot get rid of any of them, which is the price of the gift and not a choice
reports nothing about the square metre and has therefore made eleven surveys quietly false
cannot distinguish a specific residue from a general one, and knows it, and keeps reading
will accept payment for a reading he has not finished, because refusing would end the arrangement that pays him
personality.voice: Soft, slow and technical, with a professional habit of describing a reading as a place rather than as a conclusion. Very long pauses, and no impatience in them at all.
taboos: will not read a body that has not been declared and paid for
will not give a reading twice in the same words, because a repeated reading is a citable one
refuses to be thanked for a certification he does not believe
will not wash the arm twice, because the second washing is where a reading would be lost

relationships.note: The household holds the exhausted face as a title and keeps the claim by measuring it and keeping the marks legible, because an unmeasured claim is not a claim. He is the measurement and eleven of his readings on one square metre are not legible.
The face took the ground's other records with it, which is the reason a private document became a public authority, and it is the only place his sister is legible to him at all.

That account holds the grief was arithmetic, one exhausted caging ore against a frame with no spatial law seated, and it is uncontested by anybody with standing. A seam that still carries a cultivator's residue is a small piece of standing nobody has tested.

Waste does not disperse here, so forty years of heap has to be carried out by hand before a face can advance a foot, and the guild pays by the weight on a public tally. He is one of the hands and the tally does not have a column for what a hand absorbs.

A public count of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it, because it is a weight and not a distance. A reader employed to find where a seam is not does not move spoil and is not on it, which is how his season's work is unpaid.

That household keeps the divergence between the frame's reading of a life and the village's memory and records it rather than resolving it. He keeps a divergence of his own and has recorded eleven readings instead.

The conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so the reservoir gate is not blocked but meaningless: nowhere to put qi that is not moving. He is the setting's memory and its scavenger, which is why every graveyard ends up with the same people near it.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot store anything, so cannot be spent out, and cannot be frightened by a thing he has already read. Fights the way a scavenger fights: never quickly, never away, and never while standing next to something dead.
strengths: reads a corpse's residue better than a living cultivator can be read, so a body that has just died tells him everything and a body that is fighting tells him nothing
no reservoir means nothing to drain, so no exhaustion technique exists against him
almost no muscle and a marrow-heavy skeleton, so he is very hard to injure and very hard to hurry
unaffected by anything that works through the meridians, because his conduit never passes through a dantian at all
weaknesses: cannot hold a reserve, so everything he does costs him immediately and there is no second wind
almost no muscle, which means no leverage, no grappling and nothing to throw anybody with
carries permanent residue, so a heavy practitioner who dies near him makes him measurably different and slower to read
three-fingered hands built for opening rather than holding, which rules out half the available weapons
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not kill anything near him, because a body that dies beside him changes him and you cannot predict how. Fight him slowly and away from the dead, and understand that the only thing you can take from him is the ground he is standing on.
notes: He is not on the heap tally, which means the guild has been getting his season's reading free.
Eleven readings of one square metre is a survey defect and a private grief at the same time, and only he knows which is which.

appearance.presentation: A lanternfolk body in which the fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom: lighter, colder and entirely inert. She is her parent's species with the lights gone and something instead, and every instrument in the setting measures her as a control.
appearance.age: Ninety-one, which for a lanternfolk parent would be young and for her is closer to the whole of the species' life, because the bloom cost the colony's two centuries.
appearance.build: Long and light, a lanternfolk frame grown around a silicate lattice instead of a colony, with no glow, no warmth and a frame that does not regenerate anything.
appearance.complexion: Cold, faintly waxy and noticeably paler than a lanternfolk, with a fine mineral sheen at the shoulders and a translucence at the throat where the bloom replaced what was there.
appearance.hair: Pale, dry and thin, the colour the colony's light used to bleach it to, so she carries the evidence of a body she no longer has.
appearance.eyes: Dark, dry and unlit. There is nothing behind them now, which is why the mind path is open to her, and it is the only thing about her body that anybody is pleased about.
appearance.palette: Cold bone, waxy grey and a faint mineral blue at the shoulders, with one dark wool coat the only heavy value. Nothing in the design emits light, which is the whole design.
appearance.attire: A high-collared wool coat over bound linen, sleeves full and wrists closed, cut for a body that no longer produces its own warmth. She wears it indoors.
appearance.marks: A fine lattice of silicate visible at the temples and down the forearms, and a burn scar at one wrist from the year the colony died in her.
appearance.bearing: Very still and very cold, sitting rather than standing when she can, because a frame with no metabolism behind it is a frame that gets cold and stays cold.

canon.role_in_story: The only living member of a household formed by the famine, and the only one long-lived enough to be told the reason the household still eats to rule. The rule was learned before anybody could ask why, so it is carried as habit and cannot be argued out of a child; she is the last person alive who can be given the reason and cannot be given the relief.
canon.first_appearance: First seen serving a table set to the worst year's portions, in a coat she is wearing indoors, declining the larger plate she is entitled to while two people who grew up after the famine eat as much as they like.
canon.lore: A deadlight is a lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost the species its two hundred and fifty years and handed back the mind path because a body with no colony answering ahead of the question finally has an unmediated interior. It is the control case: everything the colony did and everything it prevented, recorded on one body where both can be measured. The Cinder Marked households still hold themselves to the eating rules of the year there was nothing to eat, and a household that eats to rule cannot take a larger share than the worst year allowed, which is a real ceiling on every child it raises.
history: Born a lanternfolk, and lit from inside, in a household that had already been eating by rule for two generations without knowing it was a rule.
Lost the colony at thirty-one and replaced it with a mineral bloom, which is a death and a recovery in the same event and cost her a hundred and sixty years of the species' span.

Found, at forty, that she could sit and look at her own attention, which no living member of her household had ever been able to do and which is the only thing anybody has ever been pleased about her body.
Was told, at fifty-eight, by the oldest member of the household, why the table is set the way it is, and understood that being told ends the reason and does nothing to the rule.
Became, at sixty-five, the only person in the household old enough to be told a reason and the only one too old to be argued out of it, which is the arrangement's own trap closing.

personality.summary: Cold-handed, warm-voiced, entirely unpersuadable about the rule and privately certain that the rule is wrong. She has spent thirty years with an interior nobody in her household has ever had and has used almost all of it to think about a table.
traits: keeps the household's worst-year portions without being asked and without any visible effort
explains the rule to children as a rule, and does not soften it, and hates herself for not softening it
uses the mind path constantly and involuntarily, because an unmediated interior is not a thing she can switch off
speaks warmly in a cold body, which reads as a performance and is a metabolism
has never once eaten a larger plate, in thirty years, and has never explained why to an adult
mannerisms: rubs her hands before touching anything, and apologises for the cold once and never again
serves other people's portions first without appearing to think about it
sits when she could stand, and stands when she must, with visible small discomfort in both
goes quiet at the phrase worst year, every time, including when she is the one saying it
motivations: wants the rule to be kept for a stated reason rather than an unstated one, even though the reason is gone
wants to be the person who breaks it, so that the breaking is a decision and not a collapse
wants somebody outside the household to ask why the table is set that way and be refused an answer
wants her body measured properly, since she is the control case and has been treated as an inconvenience
wants to know whether the bloom is a variant or a death, and has decided she would rather it was a death
wants to be warm, which is the one thing her body will now never do, and has stopped saying so
flaws: keeps a rule she knows is wrong, on the grounds that the alternative is worse, which is a real argument and not a resolution
cannot be argued out of it and has therefore never had the conversation she has trained herself for
carries the reason as a private burden rather than as a household's, so the household gets the rule and she gets the truth
lets being the control case make her agreeable to measurement, and agrees to readings she should refuse
personality.voice: Warm, quick and entirely unexpected from a cold-faced body, with a dry edge that arrives when she is being precise about a rule. Speaks to children more slowly than to adults and never raises her voice at either.
taboos: will not take a portion larger than the worst year allowed, in any circumstance, including a ceremony
will not explain the reason to a child, because the rule is stronger than the reason and the reason would be the worse lesson
refuses to be measured as an inconvenience or as a curiosity
will not be told she is an example, which is what every instrument in the setting calls her

relationships.note: The household applies the year's portioning to every table including the ones that now have enough, and a household that eats to rule cannot take a larger share than the worst year allowed. She is the last member who knows that the rule was ever a response to anything.

A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice where the hyphal colony was, lighter and colder and entirely inert. It reached sixty because the colony is what keeps a lanternfolk alive for two and a half centuries, and it can take the mind path for exactly the same reason.

The parent species outsourced its nervous system to a luminous colony and has no unmediated interior left to cultivate. She has one, and paid a hundred and sixty years of her span for it, and neither of those facts has ever made anybody in her household glad.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said and the village as it remembers, and the famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present. She is the household that has not been corrected and the register that would correct it, in one body.

The college keeps the burnt list so the record of a life is also the record of a gate that was never available to it. It has measured her against her species twice and found the variant both times, and has never once asked what the measurement is for.

The dosing schedules were consumed by the crisis they existed to answer, so what survived is a household habit with the arithmetic removed. She holds the reason the tables were set and not a single figure that would have set them.

A population whose fuel was its own body thinning at exactly the rate it could not stop, buying speed out of lifespan. Her species spent two centuries of lifespan on a symbiosis it did not choose, and she is the variant where it stopped.

reference_stats.summary: The only body in the setting with an unmediated interior and no regeneration whatsoever, so she thinks better than anything nearby and tires worse than anything nearby. Fights with an interior nothing can get in behind, in a frame that does not recover.
strengths: a mind path that is genuinely open, where every lanternfolk is closed, so nothing can answer ahead of her question
a body with no colony and no reservoir habit, so nothing that works through a symbiosis has anything to work on
cold to the touch and thermally inert, which makes fire-work and heat-work either useless or a gift depending on who is holding it
completely unafraid of the dark and of anything that requires a body to stay warm
weaknesses: no metabolic warmth at all, so she is a cold body in a fight that lasts and it never stops mattering
the bloom does not regenerate and the species parent does, so every wound is permanent and every second counts
no pair of eyes on her that can read a corridor before she enters it, because the reading apparatus died with the colony
sixty years of life in a setting where the useful span is two centuries, which is the whole cost of what she can do
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not wait her out and do not try to read her, because there is nothing behind the reading to interrupt. Come at her cold, come at her once, and understand that anything that requires patience will end with her hands not working properly.
notes: She is the setting's control case and has been measured as a curiosity rather than as a measurement.
Her span is a hundred and sixty years shorter than her parent's and the interior that bought it is the only reason nobody mourns the trade.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low, cold-adapted frame with heavy subcutaneous fat and a lowered core temperature, built to pack a winter as body rather than as qi. He reads as expensive, patient and slow to start.
appearance.age: Ninety-four of a hundred-and-sixty-year span, which for the species is a working adult and which he has banked against in every way a cold-climate body can.
appearance.build: Broad and low with reduced limb length and heavy fat, warm-blooded and cheap to run, and heavier than he looks by a season's worth of stored reserve.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly ruddied across the cheeks, with the coarse skin of somebody who has spent decades in weather that does not forgive.
appearance.hair: Thick, dark going grey at the temples, and cut short at the back because a cold-climate body loses heat from anywhere it is left exposed.
appearance.eyes: Pale blue, steady, and slow to focus on anything that has moved. They are the warmest thing about him.
appearance.palette: Slate, oxblood and undyed wool, with the single bright value a pair of brass weights in his hand, which are the standing weight and not jewellery.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of doubled wool with fur at the collar, sleeves full and wrists strapped, over bound linen, and heavy boots resoled so many times the sole is layered like paper.
appearance.marks: A band of hard, glossy skin across both palms where the cold has killed the surface repeatedly, and a healed frostbite notch on one ear.
appearance.bearing: Slow, heavy and immensely difficult to hurry, with the deliberate movement of a man who knows exactly how much of the season he has left in him.

canon.role_in_story: The person who has been quietly underwriting the other house's season for longer than any member of the network has been alive, and the only participant in a marriage network whose exposure is in a document. The network keeps risk in both directions so neither house has to hold enough unpriced cover, and he has been the cover.
canon.first_appearance: First seen setting a pair of brass weights down on a table between two houses and declining, when asked, to state a figure, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing in the market for a season.
canon.lore: The Dry Salt network is six marriages kept open across two counting houses, renewed whenever the houses would otherwise stop speaking, and it exists instead of a merger because an underwriter merged with a counting house is an underwriter with a price, and a price is a claim somebody can buy. What it buys is risk in both directions, so neither house has to hold enough unpriced cover to survive a bad season. What it pays is that every marriage is a disclosure, so the network is only as private as the smallest house in it. The standing weight is the measuring discipline of a people whose civic vocabulary has no word for price: weigh, never quote, and let nobody make the first offer.
history: Came south out of a cold range with a body that packs a season rather than a reserve, and was hired to carry cover on a caravan because a cold body is cheap to run.
Was married into the network in the season it was renewed, and told plainly that every marriage in it is a disclosure and that he would be the smallest house in it.
Found, in his second year, that the other house's season was not covered by anybody and that no figure for it existed anywhere because nobody was permitted to state one.
Began covering it in weight rather than in coin, which is the only instrument the standing weight permits and the only one a document can record.
Has now been the only written exposure in the network for longer than any member has been alive, and cannot stop, because stopping would require naming what he has been covering.

personality.summary: Unhurried to the point of inert, scrupulous about the distinction between weighing and quoting, and carrying a liability he cannot discharge in any of the three forms available to him.
traits: never states a figure first, in any context, for any reason
counts in weight and only in weight, and will convert to nothing
answers a direct question about his exposure with a question about whose standing is being read
takes longer to reach a decision than anybody finds reasonable and never revises one
will not be thanked, because a thanked guarantee is a guarantee somebody could decline
mannerisms: sets a brass weight down before he answers anything at all
warms his hands on a cup without appearing to notice he is doing it
says a household's name before its standing, every time
lets a silence run out rather than filling it with a price
motivations: wants the cover converted into something the network's own rules permit, and to know whether anything does
wants the smallest house in the network to be somebody other than himself
wants his exposure unrecorded without being repudiated, which are different requests and only one of them is available
wants one season where the other house covers its own road and finds out what the network is for
flaws: carries a liability he can neither name, withdraw or transfer, and calls the arrangement an arrangement
uses the rule against first offers as a reason never to disclose his own position
will not be a member of the household he underwrites, and has therefore no standing to be asked by it
has let a discipline about fairness become a way of never being the one who is named
personality.voice: Low, slow and level, with a cold-climate flatness that makes warmth sound like an affectation. Answers in weights and periods and never in figures, and treats that as ordinary rather than as evasive.
taboos: will not state a price first, to anybody, for any good
will not be recorded as a member of the household he covers
refuses to withdraw his cover, because withdrawal is a disclosure with his name on it
will not convert a weight into a figure, even for himself

relationships.note: Six marriages kept open across two counting houses, renewed whenever the houses would otherwise stop speaking, buying risk in both directions so neither has to hold enough unpriced cover. He is the cover and the smallest house in the network at once.

The counting house underwrites a caravan against the road closing, a risk no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season. He holds cover against that risk personally, and the company's name is the only reason nobody has asked for figures.

No debt owed by a named person may be written down, and the prohibition binds the prohibition's own members first. He cannot write down what he owes and therefore cannot discharge it, and the Assembly that forbids the ledger is the only body that would have received it.

The unit is mass and only mass, and nobody makes the first offer because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing for a season. His cover is the only liability in the network expressed in the one unit that cannot be used against its holder later.

One house published technique for discretion and the counting house answers access with a ledger, and the prize, who may keep a record, cannot be split because one answer is the other's reason to be raided. He keeps a figure nobody is permitted to hold, which is the dispute with a person inside it.

That house offers credit, safe-conduct and trading posts against exclusivity, and a member may not carry a rival's goods. His cover exists because that exclusivity makes a rival's road unpriceable, and his refusal to name a figure is the only thing that keeps the two arrangements apart.

The flank vessels need two warm gradients held at once and a longwinter only has one, briefly, in summer. He reaches far, never stays there, and has spent his life at a distance for exactly the reason his body cannot hold two.

reference_stats.summary: Stores the season as body rather than as qi, so he is very hard to exhaust and has nothing to draw on when the reserve is already spent. Fights like a winter: slow to start, and much longer than the other side expected.
strengths: heavy stored fat and a lowered core, so exhaustion techniques cost a longwinter almost nothing
broad, low and difficult to turn or shift, which makes him very hard to put anywhere he does not want to be
reaches far higher than the ground he is standing on and holds it for as long as the season lasts
a cold frame that shrugs off fire-work while the second gradient holds
weaknesses: needs two warm gradients at once for the flank gates and only has one, so everything he reaches for arrives late and leaves late
the store is spent once and does not refill inside a fight, so he is strongest at the beginning and worst at the end of any engagement
no warm second gradient means a cold snap costs him his ceiling mid-exchange
reduced limb length and heavy mass make him genuinely slow, and anything that punishes delay punishes him absolutely
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight a summer's gradient and then wait out the night. Force the exchange early, while his store is full, because everything after the temperature drops is a longwinter losing the only advantage his species has.
notes: He is the only written exposure in a network whose whole argument is that nobody's should be written.
The season he is covering is not the season he is standing in, which is the difference between an insurer and a debtor.
